# Sanitizer Matrix & Disk Constraints Checklist: Comprehensive live QuickFIX interop conversation

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the four-configuration matrix, the TSan bring-up clause, the targeted-build requirement, and the disk-preflight contract (FR-021…FR-023b, D-1…D-11).
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) §Disk preflight · [contracts/disk-preflight.md](../contracts/disk-preflight.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

> ⚠️ The disk gate is itself an instance of the instrument-integrity class: the reading a builder would
> naturally take (`df` inside WSL) is blind to the constraint that actually binds. These items test
> whether the requirements make that non-obvious enough to survive an implementer's common sense.

## Configuration Vocabulary

- [x] CHK001 Is the four-config set (`normal`, `asan`, `ubsan`, `tsan`) stated once normatively, with every artifact carrying the old three-value vocabulary enumerated for correction? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021a] — **SPEC-FIXED**: **applied at `spec.md`:934 (FR-021a) and `spec.md`:99 (the Gate-A-round-1 Q&A twin), widened to the CLASS rather than to a list of the artifacts found today.** FR-021a now reads *"THE CARVE-OUT IS A CLASS, NOT THAT ONE FILE. An artifact that **records a past run's configuration label** — `tests/interop/cell_results.yaml`, the evidence cells in `spec/behaviors-and-limitations.md` and `spec/feature-catalogue.md`, and any other such record — states something that was true of the run it describes, and this feature does not re-characterise it. Only artifacts that **prescribe the vocabulary going forward** are corrected: `run_interop_cell.py`'s `CONFIG_TO_PRESET`, the schema check's `CONFIGS`, and the two harness design documents."* ⚠️ **Named as a class deliberately, with the reason stated in place** — an enumeration of the artifacts found today is the next round's finding; the class stays decidable for the next artifact discovered carrying the retired label. `spec.md`:99 points at FR-021a as the carve-out's normative home rather than restating the split. ⚠️ **Unrequested consistency edit, disclosed**: `plan.md`:662 carried the same claim at its narrow width, so it now points at FR-021a too — leaving it narrow while the spec widened is the two-sites-one-fix shape. ⛔ Its *"belongs in a filed issue, not in this feature"* sentence is **byte-identical** and untouched: that is CHK003's territory, and CHK003 is excluded from this pass. ⛔ **SUPERSEDED BY ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION — the widening above was REJECTED and reverted.** The proposal rested on FR-021a's premise that `cell_results.yaml` holds historical `asan-ubsan` rows. **Measured: it does not** — 89 rows, every one `config: normal`; its only `asan-ubsan` string is a prescriptive comment (line 12, now corrected). A sweep of the parent harness found the label **only** in prescriptive artifacts. Widening a carve-out built on a nonexistent corpus would have extended a false premise to two more files **and exempted the only two genuine overclaims from being fixed**. What actually existed: `run_interop_cell.py` mapped `asan-ubsan` → the **ASan-only** preset, so `spec/behaviors-and-limitations.md` and `spec/feature-catalogue.md` credited UBSan coverage that never ran. Both are now **corrected, not exempted**; FR-021a and `plan.md` state the real distinction. ⚠️ Recorded rather than silently reverted, so the widening is not re-proposed next round.
- [x] CHK002 Is the mapping from configuration name to build preset specified as a value, so that a preset which does not enable what its name claims is a defect rather than a judgment call? [Measurability, Plan §External obligations] — PASS: `spec.md:895-896` (FR-021) gives the map as a literal value — `normal→linux-clang-debug`, `asan→linux-clang-asan`, `ubsan→linux-clang-ubsan`, `tsan→linux-clang-tsan` — restated identically at `plan.md:616`, and FR-021 ties the `asan` name to a checkable fact (`cmake/Sanitizers.cmake` sets `-fsanitize=address` and `-fsanitize=undefined` from **independent** `if()` blocks, so a preset can be inspected against its own name). A non-PASS would read "each config maps to an appropriate sanitizer preset" with no named directories — leaving "appropriate" to the implementer's judgment, exactly the ambiguity that let `asan-ubsan` ship silently ASan-only in the first place.

[Clarity, Plan §External obligations] — **SPEC-FIXED (PROPOSED)**: the out-of-scope rule itself is stated clearly (`spec.md:905-907`, `plan.md:647-649`), but "it is a filed issue, not this feature's work" (`spec.md:906`) names **no issue number**, and nothing in `tasks.md` files one — checked live: `gh issue list --state open --search "asan-ubsan"` returns nothing, and none of the 12 currently-open issues (`209,217,263,274,276,296,310,409,411,412,413,416`) covers it. Every other "filed as an issue" claim in this bundle's own lineage (see `CLAUDE.md`'s changelog: "Filed as **#252**", "spun off **#303**") names the number precisely so the claim is checkable; this one is a clause of the shape the bundle's own **RC-A**/completion rule (`plan.md:547-564`) exists to catch — a constraint stated with no producer. **Proposed edit**: add a `tasks.md` step (and an External-obligations row, since filing a tracked issue is RC-B's "work outside the bundle") that files the issue via `gh issue create` and records the resulting number back into `spec.md:906`/`plan.md:647` in the same edit — not a reword of the sentence, which would just replace one unverifiable claim with another.
  - ⛔ **RESOLVED WITHOUT FILING ANYTHING — the proposal above was rejected because BOTH premises of the deferred clause were false.** The auditor established the first (no such issue exists — confirmed independently). Orchestrator verification established the second: **there is no corpus to re-characterise.** `tests/interop/cell_results.yaml` holds **89 rows, every one `config: normal`**, and no `asan-ubsan` row at all; its single occurrence of the label is a prescriptive comment on line 12. A sweep of the parent harness found the label **only** in prescriptive artifacts (`run_interop_cell.py`, `INTEROP-016-DESIGN.md`, `INTEROP-COVERAGE-REPORT.md`, `INTEROP-016-P1-FINDINGS.md`) — **zero recorded result rows anywhere**.
  - **Applied instead**: the false premise and the *"it is a filed issue"* clause are **deleted** at both sites (`spec.md` FR-021a, `spec.md`:99 Q&A twin, `plan.md`), the prescriptive comment at `cell_results.yaml:12` is corrected to the four-config vocabulary, and the two artifacts that genuinely overclaimed — `spec/behaviors-and-limitations.md` and `spec/feature-catalogue.md`, which read *"green under `normal` + `asan-ubsan`"* while `run_interop_cell.py` mapped that key to the **ASan-only** preset — now state the preset that actually ran, keeping the historical label. **User decision, 2026-09-10: no GitHub issue is filed**, because with the premise corrected and the two lines fixed there is no residual work for one to track.

Re-derive with `grep -o "config: [a-z-]*" tests/interop/cell_results.yaml | sort | uniq -c`.

## TSan Bring-Up

- [x] CHK005 Is TSan specified as **bring-up, not a config flip**, with the distinction made concrete rather than asserted? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022] — PASS: FR-022 (`spec.md:908-912`) attaches operational teeth to the label — a TSan run that "skips, aborts during setup, or produces no witnesses MUST NOT be recorded as a pass," and any finding is "a real defect until disproven; none may be dismissed as a test artifact without a reproduction or a client-path analysis" — cross-checked by SC-011's witness-set equality gate. Non-PASS would be FR-022 stopping at "TSan is bring-up" with no consequence distinguishing it from any other config's pass/fail rule.
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for the case where the TSan arm does not come up at all — specifically that this is a **finding to record and resolve**, not grounds to mark the arm `n/a`? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-022] — PASS: Edge Cases (`spec.md:374-377`) states this exactly — *"It may not come up at all… That outcome is a finding to record and resolve, not a reason to mark the arm `n/a`."* Non-PASS would leave the failure-to-launch case unaddressed, letting an implementer default to the existing `n/a`/`deferred:*` vocabulary FR-014a's status enum already offers.
- [x] CHK007 Is the mechanism by which instrumentation could break a passing session (timing changes moving heartbeat and test-request cadence) stated, so a failure is diagnosable rather than mysterious? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases] — PASS: same Edge Cases entry (`spec.md:375-376`) names the mechanism explicitly — *"timing changes under instrumentation can move heartbeat and test-request cadence enough to break a session that passes under `normal`."* Non-PASS would state only "TSan may fail" with no causal hook, leaving a future implementer to rediscover the mechanism from scratch under time pressure.
- [x] CHK008 Are the requirements clear that only fixpp is sanitizer-instrumented and the counterparties run as unmodified binaries? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023] — PASS: FR-023 (`spec.md:913-915`) states this as the requirement's whole content. Non-PASS would be ambiguity over whether the QuickFIX counterparty binaries are rebuilt per sanitizer config — they are not (confirmed also at `plan.md:631`'s row: `interop-matrix.yml` `docker cp`s a prebuilt counterparty binary rather than rebuilding it).
- [x] CHK009 Is the **second bound** required to be stated wherever a sanitizer result is reported, rather than once in the spec? [Coverage, Spec §FR-023b] — PASS: FR-023b (`spec.md:925-930`) states the "wherever reported" scope explicitly, and this is not a bare declaration — it has a producer: `tasks.md:256` (T097) "State FR-023b's second bound wherever a sanitizer result is reported" and `quickstart.md:158` both instantiate it. Non-PASS would be FR-023b asserting the scope with no task or quickstart step realizing it — the RC-A "constrained but unproduced" shape this bundle is otherwise careful about.
- [x] CHK010 Are requirements defined for showing each sanitizer arm **genuinely ran** the conversation, as distinct from reporting clean? [Measurability, Spec §SC-011] — PASS: SC-011 (`spec.md:1210-1215`) gives a measurable, non-tautological criterion — each config's witness-set projection must equal `normal`'s and the 100-key census, via FR-015c's completeness gate; "a configuration yielding no witnesses is a failure" even though it would exit 0. Non-PASS would be SC-011 reading only "TSan/UBSan must pass," which a config producing zero witnesses (and thus reporting no findings) would trivially satisfy.

## Disk Preflight — Predicate Design

- [x] CHK011 Are the two predicates specified as evaluated **independently**, with the failure mode of collapsing them into one stated? [Clarity, Contract §D-1] — PASS: D-1 states independence directly, and `contracts/disk-preflight.md` § *Why D-1 is two predicates and not a minimum* gives the collapse failure mode in full — `min(a,b) ≥ T` fails toward a **false RED**, while a single threshold (derived from the host delta) applied to the build-mount reading is the actual, dangerous fail-open. Non-PASS would state independence as a bare assertion with no account of why the tempting alternative (a minimum) is wrong — which is exactly the shape this contract explicitly rejects.
- [x] CHK012 Is the output required to **name the failing predicate**, rather than reporting a generic failure? [Measurability, Contract §D-1a] — PASS: D-1a — *"The output names the failing predicate — `internal`, `host`, or `both`"* — echoed in `data-model.md:554,574-575` (`failing_predicate` enum field) and armed by RED arms A-1/A-1a. Non-PASS would be a bare "exit non-zero on failure" with no discriminating output field, making A-1 vs A-1a unobservable.
- [x] CHK013 Is the requirement that the gate **exit non-zero and refuse the build** stated together with its negatives — no warn-and-continue, no exit 0 on the failing path? [Clarity, Contract §D-5] — PASS: D-5 states this verbatim, with an explicit historical citation of the local anti-pattern ("the repository has a recorded gate that warns, prints `DIAGNOSTIC ONLY`, and exits 0"). Non-PASS would state only "the gate must fail" with no exclusion of the warn-and-continue shape this repo has actually shipped before.
- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for an unreadable or absent host mount on WSL as a **FAIL**, never `proceed`? [Edge Case, Contract §D-3] — PASS: D-3 — *"On WSL, an unreadable or absent host mount ⇒ FAIL. Never `proceed`"* — armed by RED arm A-3, paired with control arm A-4 (off-WSL) specifically so neither arm alone can satisfy the rule by accident. Non-PASS would leave the unreadable-mount case unstated, defaulting (per the contract's own framing) toward the dangerous direction.
- [x] CHK015 Is the off-WSL case specified as a **different** case rather than as a degenerate one, so that skipping the host predicate there does not weaken the WSL rule? [Consistency, Contract §D-4] — PASS: D-4 states it is "a *different* case, on a different code path," and `data-model.md:583-585` restates "a distinct case from unreadable, and the two must not share a code path" — with RED/control arm pair A-3/A-4 existing precisely to prove the two paths are not merged. Non-PASS would be D-3 and D-4 sharing one code path keyed only on "host mount present or not," collapsing "off WSL" and "on WSL but broken" into one outcome.
- [x] CHK016 Is the host mount required to be resolved **independently**, with fallback to the build mount named as a violation? [Completeness, Contract §D-10] — PASS: D-10 — *"The host mount is resolved independently; it may not fall back to the build mount"* — armed by spurious-hit RED arm A-8 (host mount resolves to the build mount) with its own required diagnostic (D-10, not a generic failure). Non-PASS would leave the fallback path unaddressed, letting an implementer silently satisfy the host predicate with the build-mount reading whenever `/mnt/e` cannot be resolved.
- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for an unset or unparseable threshold as a **hard error, never 0**? [Edge Case, Contract §D-9] — PASS: D-9 — *"An unset or unparseable threshold is a hard error, never 0"* — armed by spurious-hit RED arm A-7, and cross-referenced from FR-018's guard table (`spec.md:882`). Non-PASS would leave an unset threshold undefined, letting an implementer default it to `0`, which makes `proceed` vacuously true.
- [x] CHK018 Is the exclusion of the ccache device from both readings stated with the reason (a different device whose free space is not the constraint)? [Clarity, Contract §D-11] — PASS: D-11 states the exclusion and the reason — different device (`/dev/sde` vs `/dev/sdd`), backing file not on `E:` — and `plan.md:251-260` gives the operational consequence (evidence root survives `rm -rf build/<preset>`). Non-PASS would state only "exclude `/mnt/wsl/fixppbuild`" with no reason, leaving a future editor unable to tell whether the exclusion still holds if the mount layout changes.
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements defined for the reserve ballast **not** being counted as available, and for refilling it if spent? [Coverage, Plan §Reserve ballast] — **SPEC-FIXED**: **applied at `tasks.md`:61 — a new task, T002a, which is the missing PRODUCER of a rule `plan.md`:146-147 already carried.** *"Refill the reserve ballast — the half of `plan.md` § *Reserve ballast* that had no producer. T002/D-8 implements 'the preflight must not count it as available'; this task implements '**if spent, it must be refilled** as an explicit task step', which nothing did."* It carries the three parts the item asked for: **(a)** check both `/mnt/e/_wsl-reserve-{1,2}.bin` are present at 5 GiB each before every preflight-gated configure/build in T095's sequencing; **(b)** refill to 5 GiB **before the next configure or build starts** if a preceding preflight consumed either — not at the end of the matrix, since the valve must be intact for the run that needs it; **(c)** ⛔ a spent-and-unrefillable valve is a **`stop`** per `plan.md` § *When the preflight cannot be satisfied*, never a warn-and-continue, on the same rule D-5 states for the gate itself. The task also requires the check's result be recorded either way, so *"we did not need it"* does not discharge it. ⚠️ **No § *External obligations* row was added, deliberately**: `plan.md`:146-147 already carries the obligation and the ballast files are host state rather than a repo artifact this feature changes — what was missing was the producer, not the MUST-clause, so RC-B is not triggered. ⚠️ **Id form**: `T002a` rather than a renumber — the bundle's own `a`-suffix idiom (FR-021a, SC-009a, E-7a); renumbering T003…T110 would rot every task citation in the bundle to fix an ordering nobody reads.

## Threshold Provenance

- [x] CHK020 Are both required values required to come from **measurement**, per configuration, against the **targeted** build — not from an estimate or a round number? [Measurability, Contract §D-7] — PASS: D-7 states this exactly, sourcing both values from R-1's measurement "per configuration… against the targeted interop-driver build," each dated. `research.md`'s R-1 gives the full experiment design (build each config from clean, targeted, sampling both `df` readings). Non-PASS would be D-7 permitting an "estimated" or "round number" threshold outside the one explicitly scoped bootstrap exception (D-9a).
- [x] CHK021 Is the rule that `required_host_growth` may **not** be derived from or offset against the internal figure stated explicitly? [Clarity, Contract §D-7a] — PASS: D-7a states the rule and its reason precisely — the gate "may not derive it from, or offset it by, the already-materialised reuse pool," because that pool is "a bound, not a measurement," and its size is deliberately unwritten anywhere in the bundle so it cannot be subtracted. Non-PASS would leave the reuse-pool computation as a permitted shortcut, reproducing the exact under-checked-ceiling failure D-1's own rationale names.
- [x] CHK022 Are the measurement values required to carry their **date**, given that they move? [Completeness, Contract §D-6] — PASS: D-6 — *"Print both readings, both required values with their measurement dates… on every invocation"* — and D-7 — *"each recorded with its date, because these move."* Non-PASS would require the values without a date, making a stale threshold indistinguishable from a current one at read time.
- [x] CHK023 Is the bootstrap problem — the measurement cannot run under its own gate — specified with a resolution, rather than left as a circularity? [Conflict, Contract §D-9a] — PASS: D-9a gives the full resolution (`--bootstrap` mode, `estimated, pending R-1` label printed on every line, admissible only for the R-1 experiment), and `research.md` R-1a records it as "✅ DECIDED (Gate A round 2)" with the same mechanism. Non-PASS would leave R-1's four-build measurement experiment unable to run at all under D-7/D-9's unconditional thresholds — the circularity `research.md` explicitly names as having been caught and forbidden before this resolution existed.
- [x] CHK024 Do the requirements state the mechanism (a growing VHD that does not auto-shrink) clearly enough that the reclaim procedure is understood rather than cargo-culted? [Clarity, Plan §The mechanism] — PASS: `plan.md:96-138` ("The mechanism…") states this at length with the asymmetric consequence table (free-inside vs. free-on-host). Non-PASS would state only "delete a build tree to make room" with no explanation of why that works for the internal ceiling and not the host one.
- [x] CHK025 Is it stated that deleting inside the guest frees blocks for **reuse** but does **not** return space to the host, so that "delete a build tree to give the host its space back" is excluded? [Ambiguity, Plan §The mechanism] — PASS: `plan.md:100-105` states both the "valid claim" and the excluded one verbatim: *"'delete a build config to make room' is a valid claim. 'delete a build config to give E: its space back' is not, and no task may assert it."* Also restated at `contracts/disk-preflight.md` § Reclaim and § Verdicts (`reclaim-first` never offered for a host failure, for the same reason). Non-PASS would leave "delete to reclaim" ambiguous between the two readings, which is exactly the confusion that would send an operator toward reclaim on a host-space failure it cannot fix.

## Matrix Sequencing

- [x] CHK026 Is the requirement that builds be **targeted** rather than `all` stated with its magnitude, so it reads as the primary lever rather than an optimisation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023a] — PASS: FR-023a (`spec.md:916-924`) and `plan.md:188` ("★ The build unit is TARGETED… this is the single largest lever") both frame it as primary, with a qualitative magnitude ("hundreds of executables… the matrix opens four") kept deliberately unquantified to avoid the stale-figure trap the rest of the bundle guards against — the relation, not an operand. Non-PASS would bury the targeted-build requirement inside a list of minor build-hygiene notes with no signal that it is what makes the four-config matrix fit at all.
- [x] CHK027 Are requirements defined for the sequencing constraint that all four configurations may **not** fit simultaneously, with the ordering that resolves it? [Completeness, Plan §Matrix sequencing] — PASS: `plan.md:273-330` ("★ Matrix sequencing") states the constraint and a suggested order (`normal → ubsan → asan → tsan`) with reasoning for the order (constitutional coverage first, not directory size). Non-PASS would leave the four configs' build order unconstrained, letting an implementer attempt all four trees resident at once — the condition the section exists to rule out.
- [x] CHK028 Is the reclaim order specified, together with the configuration that is **never** deleted and why? [Clarity, Plan §Reclaim procedure] — PASS, on the requirement the bundle actually makes: a fixed static order is **deliberately not** specified (`plan.md:264-266`, "re-derived with `du -sh build/*/` at the moment of reclaim — never from a remembered order," with the historical reason that a written order went stale within the day) — that is itself the specified rule, a re-derivation algorithm rather than a list, and it is a documented decision rather than a silent gap. The never-deleted config **is** named with its reason: `build/linux-clang-debug/` — "standing user rule, 2026-09-10," and because it is `normal`'s resident tree. Non-PASS would be silence on both halves, leaving an implementer free to reclaim `normal`'s tree or to invent an arbitrary order with no criterion at all.
- [x] CHK029 Are requirements defined for what happens when the preflight cannot be satisfied **even after reclaim** — stop and report, with no partial build recorded as a pass or a skip? [Edge Case, Plan §When the preflight cannot be satisfied] — PASS: `plan.md:332-337` states this exactly — "Stop and report. Do not proceed with a partial build. Do not record any resulting cell as a `pass` **or** as a `skip`." Non-PASS would leave this case to fall through to FR-016's counterparty-unavailable skip path or FR-014a's `error:enospc`, both of which are wrong classifications for a preflight refusal (no build was even attempted).
- [x] CHK030 Is a run that died on `ENOSPC` required to be distinguishable from a genuine result at every layer that records an outcome? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014a] — PASS: FR-014a mandates `error:enospc` as its own terminal state, and the same three-value enum (`completed`/`aborted`/`error:enospc`) recurs consistently across every layer that records an outcome — `data-model.md:608` (run ledger `terminal_state`), `:780` (stream terminal record, both processes), `:806` (a third occurrence), and `:454/:462` (the committed manifest's `status: pass` requirement chains to the ledger's `terminal_state: completed`). Non-PASS would be `error:enospc` present at the stream layer but silently collapsing to `fail` or `aborted` at the ledger or manifest layer, letting an infrastructure abort masquerade as a fidelity defect at the layer a catalogue row actually reads.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK031 Does any requirement in this domain quote a measured size, count or free-space figure without a date and a re-derivation recipe? [Clarity, Gap] — PASS, verified against a working instrument (an earlier sweep using `grep -n "[0-9]\+ ?[GgKkMm][iI]?[Bb]\b" … | grep -n "8\."` returned empty on **every** file including `plan.md`'s own known `≈83 G` line — a false zero, since the trailing filter can only match lines containing the literal string `8.`; re-run unfiltered and first proven to find the seed line before trusting it clean). The corrected sweep (`grep -nE '[0-9]+ ?(G|GiB|GB|Gi|K|KiB|M|MiB)\b'`) over `contracts/disk-preflight.md`, `data-model.md` (whole file), `plan.md` lines 60–340, and `spec.md` FR-021…FR-023b finds exactly: the one permitted dated illustration (`plan.md:91`, "≈83 G / ≈17 G / ≈34 G," dated 2026-09-10 one paragraph above with the `df`/`du` recipe immediately preceding it and an explicit "every one of those three figures had moved by later the same day — do not carry them forward" warning); the ballast's static 5 GiB/10 GiB config constant (`plan.md:142`, `contracts/disk-preflight.md:122` — a pre-allocation size, not a measurement subject to drift); and three occurrences inside `plan.md`'s Gate A §*disagreements* review log (lines 805, 853, 866), which the bundle's own RC-3 sweep record (line 853) explains are deliberately retained as **history inside a dated disagreement record**, distinct from a *live* claim, with every corresponding *live*-clause figure already swept (`spec.md` § Assumptions, `data-model.md` §8, `contracts/disk-preflight.md`, `plan.md`'s second illustration). `data-model.md` returns zero matches, consistent with its own "no readings recorded" self-description. Non-PASS would be any of these without a date or without a recipe one line away — none found.
- [x] CHK032 Are the gate's own RED arms specified as requirements, rather than as an appendix a reader may treat as optional? [Completeness, Contract §Required RED arms] — PASS: `contracts/disk-preflight.md` § *Required RED arms* names A-1…A-8 as required, and `plan.md`'s Constitution Check re-check (VII §3 row) confirms they are "enumerated as deliverables… not left to process." FR-017/FR-018 (`spec.md:848-882`) additionally pull the disk gate's spurious-hit requirement directly into the spec's own guard table, not only into the contract appendix. Non-PASS would be the RED arms living only in the contract with no FR cross-reference, letting `/speckit-tasks` or an implementer treat the table as informative rather than binding.
- [x] CHK033 Do the disk requirements and the promotion-ordering requirements agree on when a configuration's build tree may be reclaimed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014b] — PASS: FR-014b (`spec.md:738-743`) states the promotion command "runs **after** a configuration's 8 cells complete and **before** that configuration's build tree is reclaimed" — identical wording and timing to `plan.md`'s Matrix sequencing step 1 ("persist… → reclaim config *k* → preflight → build config *k+1*") and the Per-configuration budget table ("reclaimable… after its 8 cells have run and their evidence is persisted"), and to the External-obligations row for `promote_interop_evidence.py` ("Runs after a config's 8 cells complete and before its tree is reclaimed"). Non-PASS would be any of these three sites naming a different ordering — e.g., reclaim gated on cell completion alone, without evidence persistence — which is exactly the "deleting a build tree that still holds the only copy of a run's evidence loses the run" hazard `plan.md:315-317` calls out by name.
